findings.text: Pre-existing and outside this node's scope: the seat-record mirror that preserve_seat_records keeps for the session-end reap is never signalable. watcher_record_pids derives a record's home as directory.parent.parent, so a mirrored record's home resolves under <basetemp>/_seat-records/..., while reapable_watch_pids refuses any pid whose /proc/<pid>/environ RECKON_HOME does not resolve to that same path -- and a live producer's env names the original (pruned) home. Measured directly here: a live process with RECKON_HOME=<basetemp>/pytest-gw0/test_x0/config plus a mirrored record under <basetemp>/_seat-records/pytest-gw0/test_x0/config/crew/watch yields watcher_record_pids listing the mirrored pid but reapable_watch_pids returning []. So the mirror contributes nothing to the reap's signalling path and only the per-test reap (which reads the originals before prune) does. This does not affect this node's verdict: hiding the mirror during tests cannot change what the reap can signal. Flagged for the conftest owner, not repaired here.

justifications.durability: The mechanism is sound: join_watch_sweeps bounds each join and reports stragglers rather than waiting forever; the fixture requests tmp_path and monkeypatch so it finalizes before the temporary tree and the patched modules are torn down; the by-name join catches producers the watch claim popped from the registry. The mirror fix renames the mirror outside the run's root (the reap walks crew/watch anywhere under the root, so an inside rename would not hide it) and restores it from a session-scoped finalizer that the session-end reap outlives. I checked the one place hiding the mirror could regress the session reap -- that the per-test reap signals producers through mirrored records -- and measured that it does not (mirrored records are refused by the home check), so the content reduction is inconsequential; see the follow-on finding on the pre-existing mirror. Held at 19 rather than full because the mirror fixture discards the previously-aside mirror at every setup, so the session-end reap sees only the most recent test's mirrored set rather than the accumulated one -- harmless given the measurement, but an unstated change in what a backstop can see.

The population arms are readable (110 then 113 passed, both EXIT=0). Held below full for one wording defect: the declared negative-control string says 'head without the autouse fixture', but the run's log header applies 'base plus the node test file only' (no helper and no fixture), so the log as filed does not demonstrate the declared mutation exactly; I closed that gap with my own run of the declared mutation, which fires, but the record should have applied what it declared.
